article_title: Simulation-based training and assessment of mobile pre-hospital SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic teams in Styria, Austria.
citation: Mileder LP, Schüttengruber G, Prattes J, Wegscheider T. (2020). Simulation-based training and assessment of mobile pre-hospital SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic teams in Styria, Austria. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000021081
title: 1-day simulation-based training curriculum for mobile pre-hospital SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic teams
description: A 375-minute curriculum combining "90 minutes of theoretical instruction (COVID-19 and hygiene)", 135 minutes of technical skills training, 90 minutes of simulator-based algorithm training emulating the whole prehospital process, and 60 minutes of OSCE assessment. It was delivered at the SIM CAMPUS simulation hospital in Eisenerz using high-fidelity patient simulation in rooms resembling a private home, for Austrian Red Cross mobile diagnostic teams.
requirements: Participants are emergency medical personnel preparing for prehospital SARS-CoV-2 testing duties; a simulation hospital setting with high-fidelity simulators is used
constraints: The schedule did not allow for a pretraining evaluation of skills, per the article's limitations section
target_learners: practicing physicians engaged with the Austrian Red Cross
target_learning_goals: correct use of personal protective equipment
collection of naso-/oropharyngeal swabs for RT-PCR testing
examples: Seven trainings were delivered between March 2nd and March 22nd, 2020, at the SIM CAMPUS simulation hospital on an area of 4000 square meters.
key_sources: Mileder LP, Schüttengruber G, Prattes J, Wegscheider T. (2020). Simulation-based training and assessment of mobile pre-hospital SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic teams in Styria, Austria. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000021081
